name: Pueblo of Tesuque grant, confirmed by Congress December 22, 1858 (Royce Area 672)
promises: Congress confirmed the Pueblo of Tesuque's land claim, as reported favorably by the Surveyor General of New Mexico, and ordered it surveyed and patented (Act of December 22, 1858, 11 Stat. 374).
The Act says the confirmation is only a relinquishment of the United States' own title and claim, and does not affect any adverse valid rights.
Royce records the grant as 17,471.12 acres, confirmed in 1858 and patented in 1864.

The Pueblo Lands Act of 1924 made the United States liable, and directed the Pueblo Lands Board to award compensation, for Pueblo land and water lost through the United States' failure to seasonably prosecute the Pueblo's rights (Section 6).
compensation: Tesuque is not among the pueblos given additional compensation in Section 2 of the Act of May 31, 1933. Section 3 of that Act paid $1,094.64 to non-Indian claimants within the Pueblo of Tesuque whose claims were not sustained, that is, land that stayed with the Pueblo.
today: No finding was found that land inside the Tesuque grant was lost under the 1924 Act or otherwise.

openQuestions: The date 1886-10-01 in treaties.json is not an event date for this land. Royce prints the Pueblo grants under a block headed 'Oct. 1, Act of Congress, Stat. L. XI, 374'; 11 Stat. 374 is the Act of December 22, 1858, which confirmed the grant. This is land the Pueblo kept, not land it ceded. Not edited.
The Pueblo Lands Board's report on Tesuque was not read; it could show grant land confirmed to non-Indians with no award. Lead for a deeper pass.
The Pueblo of Tesuque's own account was not located: pueblooftesuque.org loaded with no history text.
The statute link in treaties.json (ops.libs.uga.edu) was not used; the Act was read on govinfo.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): no-breach-found confirmed. The Act of May 31, 1933 (read on govinfo) is not counted as a breach for any Pueblo grant: it states no findings and names pueblos, not grants, and the Indian Claims Commission held in 1976 that Congress paid full market value for land lost under the 1924 Act (39 Ind. Cl. Comm. 34).

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Pueblo, Tesuque, Tesuque grant; no Tesuque Court of Claims case; the one ICC hit is Nambe Docket 358; the ICC aboriginal-title decisions found expressly exclude the confirmed grants (e.g. 30 Ind. Cl. Comm. 234, 1973), so nothing new inside this grant.
